questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The boys in the yard plays soccer every afternoon.
questions.explanation: The subject "boys" is plural, so the verb should be "play", not "plays".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
My brother and sister is studying in Manila.
questions.explanation: A compound subject joined by "and" is plural, so use "are".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The dogs barks at strangers every night.
questions.explanation: "Dogs" is plural, so the verb should be "bark".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Either the teacher or the students is responsible for the noise.
questions.explanation: With "either...or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "students", so use "are responsible".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Neither of the answers are correct according to the key.
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular, so the verb should be "is".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Economics are a required subject for all business students.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects such as "Economics" take a singular verb: "is".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Here are the documents you requested.
questions.explanation: The plural subject "documents" correctly takes "are" in the inverted sentence, so there is no error.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The quality of the products sold in the market have improved lately.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular "quality", not "products", so the verb should be "has".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
One of the reasons why she resigned were her low salary.
questions.explanation: "One" is the singular subject (and "her low salary" is singular), so the verb should be "was".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
There is several problems in the budget proposal.
questions.explanation: The real subject "problems" is plural, so use "are" after "There".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Ten thousand pesos are too much for a pair of shoes.
questions.explanation: A sum of money treated as a single amount takes a singular verb: "is".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The president, together with his cabinet members, are expected to attend the summit.
options: The president, together with his cabinet members,
questions.explanation: Phrases introduced by "together with" do not change the subject; "president" is singular, so use "is".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Not only the mayor but also the councilors was invited to the ceremony.
options: Not only the mayor but also the councilors
questions.explanation: With "not only...but also", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "councilors", so use "were".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
A number of employees has requested a salary increase.
questions.explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb, so use "have".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The number of applicants has increased this year.
questions.explanation: "The number of" takes a singular verb, so "has increased" is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Last week, we goes to the beach with our cousins.
questions.explanation: A past time marker requires the simple past: "went".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Yesterday, he buy a new bag at the mall.
questions.explanation: "Yesterday" signals the simple past: "bought".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
They have went to school already.
questions.explanation: The present perfect needs the past participle "gone", not "went".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
I am living in Davao since 2015.
questions.explanation: "Since" with a starting point requires the present perfect: "have been living" or "have lived".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
When I was a child, I often play in the river.
questions.explanation: The past habit needs the past tense: "played".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Rizal has written Noli Me Tangere in 1887.
questions.explanation: A finished action at a specific past time uses the simple past: "wrote".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The sun rises in the east every morning.
questions.explanation: A general truth uses the simple present, so "rises" is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
After she had finished her homework, she watch television.
options: After she had finished her homework,
questions.explanation: The sequence of past events needs the simple past: "watched".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
If it rains tomorrow, the class would be cancelled.
questions.explanation: A real future condition ("rains") takes "will be" in the result clause.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The teacher asked why we are late for class yesterday.
questions.explanation: After the past verb "asked", the clause shifts to the past: "we were".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
We are waiting for two hours when the bus finally arrived.
questions.explanation: An action in progress before a past event requires the past perfect progressive: "had been waiting".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
She is knowing the answer to the question.
questions.explanation: Stative verbs like "know" are not used in the progressive; use "knows".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
If she had studied harder, she would pass the exam.
questions.explanation: A past unreal condition ("had studied") needs "would have passed" in the result clause.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
By the time the rescuers arrived, the survivors are waiting for three days.
options: By the time the rescuers arrived,
questions.explanation: An action completed before a past point needs the past perfect progressive: "had been waiting".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
By the time you arrive, we will have finished dinner.
questions.explanation: The simple present in the time clause with the future perfect in the main clause is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Her and I went to the market together.
questions.explanation: A subject needs the subjective case: "She and I".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The teacher gave the books to he and his sister.
questions.explanation: The object of the preposition "to" takes the objective case: "him".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Maria and him are good friends.
questions.explanation: The compound subject needs the subjective case: "Maria and he".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Us students are going on a field trip.
questions.explanation: The subject needs the subjective case: "We students".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The dog wagged it's tail happily.
questions.explanation: "It's" means "it is"; the possessive pronoun is "its".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The boy cut hisself with a knife.
questions.explanation: The correct reflexive pronoun is "himself"; "hisself" is not standard.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The principal praised Ramon and I for our hard work.
questions.explanation: "Ramon and I" is the object of "praised", so use "Ramon and me".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The teacher gave Carlo and me extra homework.
questions.explanation: "Carlo and me" is correctly in the objective case as the indirect object.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
My sister and myself are going to Baguio.
questions.explanation: A reflexive pronoun cannot serve as the subject; use "I".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Whom is calling at this hour?
questions.explanation: "Who" is the subject of "is calling", so the subjective case is needed.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Neither of the girls brought her umbrella.
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular and the girls are female, so "her" is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The shirt that I bought it yesterday is too small.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun "that" already stands for the object, so "it" is redundant.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Whom do you think will win the election?
questions.explanation: "Who" is the subject of "will win", despite the intervening "do you think".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
She is the one whom I believe is the best candidate.
options: I believe is the best candidate.
questions.explanation: "Who" is the subject of "is the best candidate"; "I believe" is parenthetical.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Having been invited by he and his wife, we brought a gift.
questions.explanation: The object of the preposition "by" takes the objective case: "him and his wife".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
She is very good in playing the piano.
questions.explanation: The correct idiom is "good at".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The teacher explained me the lesson.
questions.explanation: "Explain" takes "to" before the person: "explained to me the lesson" or "explained the lesson to me".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
He is more taller than his brother.
questions.explanation: Do not double the comparative; use "taller".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
She is allergic at shrimp and crab.
questions.explanation: The correct idiom is "allergic to".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
We discussed about the new policy during the meeting.
questions.explanation: "Discuss" is transitive; omit "about".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Ana likes singing, dancing, and to draw.
questions.explanation: Parallelism: use "drawing" to match "singing" and "dancing".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The affect of the typhoon was devastating.
questions.explanation: The noun meaning "result" is "effect", not "affect".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The new employee is hardworking, honest, and has dedication.
questions.explanation: Parallelism: the adjectives need "dedicated" to match "hardworking" and "honest".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The report was neither accurate or complete.
questions.explanation: "Neither" pairs with "nor", not "or".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The number of less students this year worries the dean.
questions.explanation: Use "fewer" with countable nouns such as "students".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
She prefers reading novels than watching movies.
questions.explanation: "Prefer" is followed by "to", not "than".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
She is interested in learning how to cook and how to bake.
questions.explanation: The two "how to" phrases are parallel and the idiom "interested in" is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The proposal was rejected not because it was costly but because of it lacked clarity.
options: The proposal was rejected not because it was costly
questions.explanation: Parallelism: "not because it was costly but because it lacked clarity".

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
The pilot had to lay down after the long flight.
questions.explanation: The intransitive verb "lie" is needed; "lay" requires an object.

questions.question:
Choose the part of the sentence that needs correction. Choose "No error" if the sentence is correct.
Nobody was more surprised than I at the result.
questions.explanation: "Than I" is the correct formal comparison with the implied verb "was", so there is no error.

questions.question: Bumili si Ana ___ bagong damit.
questions.explanation: Ang "ng" ang pananda ng layon ("bagong damit") ng pandiwang "bumili".

questions.question: Tumakbo siya ___ mabilis.
questions.explanation: Ang "nang" ay pang-abay na naglalarawan ng paraan ng pagkilos ("nang mabilis").

questions.question: Ang bahay ___ lola ay malaki.
questions.explanation: Ang "ng" ay pananda ng pag-aari (kay lola), katumbas ng "of".

questions.question: Mabait ___ ang guro natin.
questions.explanation: Nagtatapos sa katinig (t) ang "mabait", kaya "daw" ang gamit.

questions.question: Maganda ___ ang palabas.
questions.explanation: Nagtatapos sa patinig (a) ang "maganda", kaya "raw" ang gamit.

questions.question: Masaya ___ ang kaarawan ni Lola.
questions.explanation: Nagtatapos sa patinig (a) ang "masaya", kaya "raw" ang gamit.

questions.question: Mag-aral ka ___ mabuti upang pumasa.
questions.explanation: Ang "nang" ay pang-abay na naglalarawan kung paano ang pag-aaral ("nang mabuti").

questions.question: Naghintay kami ___ ilang oras.
questions.explanation: Ang "ng" ay pananda ng layon ("ilang oras") ng pandiwang "naghintay".

questions.question: Umiyak siya ___ umalis ang kanyang ina.
questions.explanation: Ang "nang" ay katumbas ng "noong" o "when" sa pagsasaad ng panahon.

questions.question: Nagsikap siya ___ makapagtapos ng pag-aaral.
questions.explanation: Ang "nang" ay nangangahulugang "upang" o "so that" sa pagpapahayag ng layunin.

questions.question: Darating ___ si Mayor bukas.
questions.explanation: Nagtatapos sa katinig (g) ang "darating", kaya "daw" ang gamit.

questions.question: Sino ___ ang nakakita sa kanya?
questions.explanation: Nagtatapos sa patinig (o) ang "sino", kaya "raw" ang gamit.

questions.question: Tuloy ___ ang pista sa Sabado.
questions.explanation: Nagtatapos sa y ang "tuloy", at ginagamit ang "raw" kapag ang huling tunog ay patinig o w/y.

questions.question: Umalis siya ___ hindi nagpaalam.
questions.explanation: Ang "nang" ay nangangahulugang "without/when" bilang pangatnig sa "nang hindi nagpaalam".

questions.question: Bawal ___ ang pumasok dito.
questions.explanation: Nagtatapos sa katinig (l) ang "bawal", kaya "daw" ang gamit.
